pages.name: PDF Size Reducer
pages.title: Free PDF Size Reducer — shrink a PDF without uploading it
pages.description: Reduce PDF file size in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, no email, no watermark, no sign-up. Best on scanned documents, where it typically halves the size.
pages.intro: Most tools that shrink a PDF ask you to upload it to their servers first. If the document is a signed contract, a passport scan or a client's accounts, that is a decision you may not want to make. This one never sends the file anywhere.
faqs: Is this PDF size reducer really free?
Yes. There is no account, no email address, no watermark, no page limit and no paid tier hiding the useful settings. It is one of nine free instruments KaiOrb publishes.
Does my PDF get uploaded to a server?
No. The file is read and rewritten by your own browser. You can disconnect from the internet after the page loads and it still works, which is the simplest proof that nothing is being sent.
How much smaller will my PDF get?

It depends entirely on what is inside. A scanned document is mostly JPEG images and commonly halves — a one-page scan in our testing went from 84 KB to 39 KB. A PDF that is mostly text and fonts will barely change, and the tool tells you that rather than handing back a file the same size.
Will it ruin the quality?
You choose. Four quality settings run from barely-visible change to maximum compression, and a separate resolution control. Text drawn as text is never touched — only the pictures are recompressed.
Why did it refuse my file?

Three cases are refused on purpose rather than producing a broken document: encrypted PDFs, PDFs with no recompressible images, and PDFs that store their objects in a compressed structure this tool will not rewrite. Your original is never modified.
Does it work on a phone?
Yes, in any modern mobile browser. Very large scans may exhaust memory on an older phone, and if that happens the page says so instead of hanging.
guide: How to reduce PDF size without uploading it

pages.name: Photo Size Targeter
pages.title: Free Image Compressor — hit an exact KB size, no upload
pages.description: Compress a JPG, PNG or WebP to an exact file size — under 200 KB, under 50 KB — in your browser. Nothing uploaded, EXIF stripped, free with no sign-up.
pages.intro: Upload forms are unforgiving: under 200 KB, under 1 MB, exactly this or nothing. This searches quality first, then resolution, and stops at the best-looking image that still fits the number you named.
faqs: How do I compress an image to a specific KB size?

Type the limit — 200 KB, 100 KB, 50 KB — and the tool binary-searches JPEG quality between 0.05 and 0.95 to find the highest quality that still fits. If even the lowest quality is too big, it scales the image down in steps and searches again.
Is the image uploaded anywhere?
No. It is decoded and re-encoded on a canvas inside your own browser. Passport photos and ID scans never leave the machine.
Does it remove EXIF data?
Yes, as a side effect of re-encoding through a canvas. GPS coordinates and camera details in the original are not carried into the output, which matters if you are about to post the picture publicly.
Which formats can it write?
JPEG, WebP and PNG. JPEG is smallest for photographs, WebP is smaller still in modern browsers, and PNG is lossless so only its resolution can be reduced.
What if it cannot reach my target?
It says so, and shows the smallest it managed and at what dimensions, rather than silently handing back something over the limit.
guide: How to resize an image to an exact file size

pages.name: Video to Audio Converter
pages.title: Free MP4 to WAV Converter — extract audio in your browser
pages.description: Extract the audio from an MP4, MOV or WebM and save it as a WAV. Runs in your browser, nothing uploaded, free. 16 kHz mono preset for transcription.
pages.intro: Pull the sound out of a recording without handing the video to a conversion site. Useful before transcription, for podcast edits, and any time you need the audio and not the pictures.
faqs: How do I convert MP4 to WAV for free?

Drop the file in, choose a sample rate and channel count, and press Extract audio. Your browser's own decoder reads the audio track and ignores the video frames; the result is written as a standard RIFF/PCM WAV.
Is my video uploaded?
No. Everything happens in the tab. That matters for client recordings, interviews and anything under NDA.
What settings should I use for transcription?
16,000 Hz mono. That is what most speech-to-text engines expect, and it is roughly a sixth the size of CD-quality stereo. There is a preset for exactly that.
Can it output MP3?
No, and deliberately. MP3 encoding needs a licensed encoder this page does not ship. WAV is uncompressed and universally readable — convert it afterwards if you need MP3.
Why does it say there is no audio?

Either the file genuinely has no audio track — screen recordings made without a microphone often do not — or its codec is not one your browser can decode. The tool names both possibilities rather than guessing.
How large a file can it handle?
The whole track is held in memory while converting, so very long recordings can exhaust a tab. 16 kHz mono needs about a sixth of the memory of CD-quality stereo, which is usually the fix.
guide: How to extract audio from a video without uploading it

pages.name: Subnet & CIDR Calculator
pages.title: Free CIDR Subnet Calculator — IPv4 and IPv6, RFC 3021 aware
pages.description: Subnet ranges, usable hosts, netmask and broadcast for IPv4 and IPv6. Recommends a prefix for a device count and checks two blocks for overlap. Free.
pages.intro: Subnet maths is easy to get subtly wrong, and the subtle errors are the ones that reach production. This does the arithmetic exactly, in big integers, and follows the standards rather than the usual shortcut formula.
faqs: What prefix do I need for 500 devices?

Enter the device count and the recommender returns the smallest prefix that fits, with the headroom it leaves. It accounts for the addresses you cannot assign, so the number it gives is usable hosts and not raw address count.
Why does a /31 show two usable addresses?

Because RFC 3021 says so. A /31 carries two usable addresses for point-to-point links and a /32 carries one, instead of the 'minus two' that applies to ordinary subnets. Many calculators get this wrong and report zero.
Does it support IPv6?
Yes. IPv6 arithmetic uses BigInt so the counts are exact rather than rounded through floating point. IPv6 reserves no broadcast address, so every address in the prefix is usable.
Can it tell me if two subnets overlap?

Yes — the overlap check takes two blocks and reports whether one contains the other, where the shared range starts and ends, and how many addresses are involved. Worth running before committing an address plan.
Is anything sent to a server?
No. It is pure arithmetic in the browser, so your internal address plan stays internal.
guide: Subnet masks and CIDR, explained by what you actually need

pages.name: Business Finance Analyzer
pages.title: Free Burn Rate & Runway Calculator — margin and break-even
pages.description: Work out gross margin, net margin, monthly burn, runway and break-even revenue from your own figures. Runs in your browser, nothing uploaded, free.
pages.intro: Four numbers decide whether a small business is fine or in trouble: what each sale actually earns, what the month costs regardless, how long the cash lasts, and how much revenue clears the bar. This works all four out and says plainly which problem you have.
faqs: How do I calculate runway?

Cash divided by monthly burn, where burn is net profit when it is negative. If you set a growth rate this tool steps month by month instead, because growth changes the burn every month and a single division would quietly ignore that.
What is break-even revenue?

Fixed costs divided by gross margin — the sales you need before the bills that arrive anyway are covered. If your gross margin is zero or negative, break-even does not exist at any volume, and the tool says 'unreachable' rather than printing a number.
What counts as a direct cost rather than a fixed cost?

Direct costs scale with each sale: materials, payment fees, per-customer hosting, delivery contractors. Fixed costs arrive whether you sell or not: salaries, rent, tools, insurance. Putting a cost in the wrong bucket is the most common reason these numbers mislead.
Is my financial data uploaded?
No. Nothing is stored, sent or logged. Close the tab and it is gone.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is arithmetic. It does not know your tax position, receivables, seasonality or debt schedule, and it is not a substitute for an accountant.

pages.title: Free Meta Tag & Schema Generator — with live SERP preview
pages.description: Write meta and Open Graph tags with a live search and social preview, generate LocalBusiness JSON-LD, and build redirect rules. Free, in your browser.
pages.intro: Four jobs that get skipped because each is small and none is interesting: the tags that decide how a page looks in search, the structured data that tells engines what a business is, the redirects that stop a rebuild losing traffic, and a keyword list with the duplicates taken out.
faqs: How long should a meta title and description be?

Roughly 60 characters for a title and 155 for a description, and the counters flag those. Treat them as a working range rather than a rule: search engines truncate on rendered pixel width, so a title in capitals runs out of room sooner than the same count in lower case.
What is JSON-LD structured data for?

It tells a search engine what a page is about in a form it does not have to guess at — that this is a business, with this name, phone and address. This generator emits Organization, LocalBusiness, Restaurant and ProfessionalService.
Why will it not add my address?
Because a country on its own is not an address. It needs at least a street, city, region or postcode before it emits a PostalAddress — a half-filled structured-data node is worse than none.
Can it generate redirects for nginx and Netlify?
Yes, and Apache .htaccess. It also refuses to emit a rule that redirects a path to itself, and skips duplicate sources, because both fail silently in production.
Does it check my live site?
No. It fetches nothing and logs no URL. Everything is generated from what you type.
guide: Meta tags and structured data, without a developer

faqs: What is a UTM parameter and do I need one?

UTM parameters are tags on a link that tell your analytics where a visitor came from. Without them, traffic from a newsletter and traffic from a paid ad look identical, and you cannot tell which one worked.
How do I make a URL slug from a title with accents?

Paste the title. The slug generator folds accented characters to their closest ASCII equivalent, so 'Café Münchén' becomes 'cafe-munchen' rather than losing the words entirely or emitting percent-encoding.

It generates rules and flags the common mistakes, including disallowing a path you probably meant to keep crawlable. It does not fetch your live file — nothing on this page makes a network request.

No. All four tools run in the browser.

faqs: How do I make an invoice for free?

What has to be on an invoice?

The word Invoice, a unique invoice number, the date issued, your business name and address, the customer's details, itemised goods or services with quantities and unit prices, the amount of any tax, and the total. Payment terms and how to pay belong there too, or you will be chased for them.
How is an invoice different from a quote or a purchase order?

A quote is the supplier offering a price. A purchase order is the buyer committing to buy. An invoice is the supplier saying it has been supplied and is now payable. Three documents, three directions — sending the wrong one is a common reason a payment sits unprocessed.
Does the tax calculate correctly?

Discount comes off the subtotal, then tax applies to what is left. Every amount is held in whole cents from the moment you type it, so the total always equals the sum of its own rows rather than being a penny out.
Can I save it as a PDF?

Yes — press Print and choose Save as PDF. Your browser already has a competent PDF writer, so this page does not load a second one. The editor is hidden when printing, so what comes out is the invoice alone.
Does it keep a record of my invoices?

No. Nothing is saved, sent or logged, and there is no numbering sequence between visits — the number is pre-filled and you overwrite it. Keep the PDFs, or use an accounting system if you need a register.

pages.name: Margin & Markup Calculator
pages.title: Free Margin & Markup Calculator — with VAT and sales tax
pages.description: Selling price from cost and margin, or margin from cost and price. Markup and margin are different numbers and this shows both. Free, in your browser.
pages.intro: The pricing questions that cost real money when they are answered wrong.
guide: Margin is not markup, and the difference is your profit
faqs: What is the difference between margin and markup?
Margin is profit as a share of the selling price; markup is profit as a share of the cost. Cost 40 sold at 60 is a 33.3% margin and a 50% markup — the same money, two different numbers.
How do I calculate selling price from a target margin?

Price equals cost divided by (1 minus the margin). For a 40% margin on a cost of 40: 40 ÷ 0.6 = 66.67. Multiplying by 1.4 instead gives 56, which is the markup formula wearing the wrong label and the most common pricing error in a small business spreadsheet.
Can a margin be 100%?
No. Margin is a share of the price, so reaching 100% would need an infinite price. The tool says so rather than printing a number. Markup has no ceiling — a 300% markup is perfectly ordinary.
Where does VAT or sales tax fit?
On top of the selling price, after all the margin arithmetic. It changes what the customer pays and not what you make, so it is shown separately rather than folded into the margin.
Is my cost data sent anywhere?
No. What you pay your suppliers is commercially sensitive and there is no reason for it to leave the tab. Nothing is stored, sent or logged.

pages.name: Colour Contrast Checker
pages.title: Free Colour Contrast Checker — WCAG AA and AAA
pages.description: Check text contrast against WCAG AA and AAA, and get the nearest passing shade when it fails. Runs in your browser, nothing uploaded, free.
pages.intro: Accessibility questions that come up the first time someone runs an audit on your site.
faqs: What contrast ratio do I need?
4.5:1 for normal body text to meet WCAG AA, and 7:1 for AAA. Large text — 24px, or 18.66px when bold — needs 3:1 for AA and 4.5:1 for AAA. Interface components and meaningful graphics need 3:1.
How is the ratio calculated?

Each channel is converted from sRGB to linear light, relative luminance is 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B, and the ratio is (lighter + 0.05) ÷ (darker + 0.05). That is WCAG 2.1 exactly, not an approximation from perceived brightness.
My grey text fails. What is the closest colour that passes?

The tool walks your colour toward black or white — whichever direction the background allows — until it meets 4.5:1, and shows you that shade. Stepping in sRGB keeps the hue recognisably the one you chose, so it reads as a nudge rather than a redesign.
Is passing the contrast check enough to be accessible?

No. Contrast is necessary, not sufficient. It says nothing about whether colour is the only thing carrying meaning, whether text sits on a photograph where the background varies per pixel, or whether a translucent layer changes what is really behind the text.
Does it send my brand colours anywhere?
No. It is arithmetic on six hex digits, done in your browser. Nothing is fetched and nothing is logged.
